items.title: Enhanced multimodal transformer framework for sarcasm detection with particle swarm optimization based feature fusion
items.abstract: Intelligent Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) has a pivotal place in sarcasm detection, given that sarcastic utterances may have an intended meaning that is not in the literal meaning of the spoken words. Sarcasm is also difficult to spot correctly since it varies not only in text but also in voice and other visual indicators like facial expression and body language. Unimodal sarcasm detection methods are generally limited by contextual ambiguity, the insensitivity of contextual paralinguistic cues, and decreased performance in situations where one modality is noisy or incomplete. These problems may cause unpredictable results and inadequate functionality in the real conversational context. To overcome these shortcomings, for sarcasm detection, we suggest an approach with different modalities which uses multi-modal cues like audio, video as well as text to provide complementary information from various communication channels. In the case of textual representation, the RoBERTa architecture was used to elicit deep contextual and semantic features of dialog transcripts. The HuBERT architecture was used to model acoustic features and is effective at representing speech representations in terms of prosodic and tonal variation based on sarcastic speech. Simultaneously, the ViViT architecture was used to process visual data and identify both spatial and temporal patterns of facial expressions and gestures in videos. Modality-specific feature representations are then combined with a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based fusion strategy which decides best-found modality weights by minimizing classification loss. The fused representation is then optimized and then through the two-layer fully connected classifier to classify sarcasm. The suggested framework was evaluated with the publicly available MUStARD dataset. The model displayed an accuracy of 94% and the recall, precision and weighted F1-score were all equal to 0.94. Comparative evaluation also compared the proposed PSO-Multimodal Fusion Model with the unimodal models and also with the traditional multimodal fusion models such as attention-based model, Graph-based model, Generative Approach, LLM/Modeling-based model, and contrastive learning approach, and showed that the proposed multimodal fusion framework yields the highest weighted F1-score among the evaluated approaches. Experimental outcomes prove that the multimodal fusion methodology based on optimization enhances the performance of sarcasm detection in contrast to the unimodal and traditional fusion techniques, which indicate its efficiency in practical use in conversational AI.

items.title: Enhancing Decision-Making in Single-Pilot Operations Through Proactive and Explainable Human-Autonomy Teaming
items.abstract: Single-Pilot Operations (SPO) in commercial aviation raise critical safety challenges in complex, time-pressured situations where human expertise is paramount. This study investigates how AI-based Human-Autonomy Teaming (HAT) can support pilot decision-making under high workload, compromised situational awareness, and time pressure. In a high-fidelity Airbus A320 simulator, 22 airline pilots performed a fuel- and time-constrained approach scenario designed to challenge HAT’s operational effectiveness under four conditions: no assistance, on-demand AI, proactive AI, and proactive explainable AI. Workload (NASA-TLX) remained high across conditions, yet decision-making differed markedly. Without assistance, only 20% chose the safest landing option; with on-demand AI, 40%; and with proactive AI (both versions), 100%. Explainable AI yielded the highest scenario comprehension (75%), matching two-crew baseline performance. Proactive systems increased decision and SA related interactions, fostering a collaborative dynamic akin to traditional crew resource management. Thus, the results demonstrate that, in the context of SPO, proactive and explainable AI was associated with crew-level decision performance within the experimental scenario without adding cognitive load. Beyond the aeronautical domain, our results are of interest for the design of cognitive support systems for high-risk domains where teams composed of humans and AI must adapt in real time.

items.title: Enhancing Teachers’ Digital Media Competence through AI-Based Training to Support Environmental Projects and Learning
items.abstract: Teachers' limited competence in utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based digital media has hindered the effective implementation of innovative teaching practices and environmental projects. This community service program aimed to enhance teachers' knowledge and skills in developing AI-based instructional media. The program was conducted at State Senior High School 1 Koto Kampar Hulu and involved 29 teachers through educational seminars, workshops, hands-on practice, and mentoring using Canva AI, Gemini AI, and NotebookLM. Program effectiveness was evaluated using pretest-posttest assessments, N-Gain analysis, instructional media product evaluation, and participant satisfaction questionnaires. The results showed that the participants' mean score increased from 47.0 to 78.9, with an N-Gain score of 0.6, indicating a moderate level of improvement. All participants (100%) demonstrated increased knowledge following the training. Furthermore, every participant successfully developed at least one AI-based instructional medium, such as a poster or infographic, that was ready for implementation in classroom instruction and environmental projects. These findings indicate that the training effectively enhanced teachers' digital competencies and their ability to integrate AI technologies into teaching and learning practices
